current.text: He is a projected starter for the Knicks, next to Brunson, Bridges, Anunoby and Towns.
Experts expect him to stay at about 30 minutes a game. They see no return to 36 or 37 minute roles because the Knicks will be careful with his workload.
He is named the Knicks starter most at risk of decline because of past wear and tear, and he showed signs of decline last season.
The Knicks are the reigning champions.

The Knicks are expected to be conservative over the first 30 or so games, with starters' minutes trimmed and more rest on back-to-backs. Some experts also fear a small championship hangover with slightly fewer minutes and more injury risk.
The Knicks are projected to win about 50 to 54 games.
Experts see no upside at his market price. Pay no more than 2 USD; a mock auction took him at 8 USD, and ESPN draft spots of 61 to 83 are called too high.
His block rate fell last season and could move back up a little.

durable.text: He is a stat stuffer whose game relies on motor and athleticism.
He is historically a 31 to 33 percent three-point shooter.
Rebounds are his best category and are strong for a guard or forward. He also helps in assists and steals, with a solid FG%.
He played through hand injuries last season.
He is a strong perimeter defender. He slowed Castle in the Finals by shading him toward his left hand.

note: Hart is a cheap all-category filler. Yahoo and ESPN both rank him 97th, at about 2 to 4 USD. He went for 6 USD in our league last season, and the experts would not pay more than 2 USD. With no weak category flagged and about 7.8 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.2 steals projected, he fits any build as a last-dollar starter or bench piece. Do not chase him if the price climbs. Early on, check whether his minutes stay near 30 or drop further while the Knicks are cautious over the first 30 or so games.
